Subagent research: Effect-compatible agents (w45:pA, done):
**Question:** which agent options work with Effect v4 on Workers, and what is "pi durable".
Sources: T = trial/inspection of the installed package, S = source or registry metadata, D = documentation.

**"pi durable" is `@earendil-works/pi-durable`**
- Version 1.4.0, published 2026-10-21; first published 2026-09-19. S: https://registry.npmjs.org/@earendil-works/pi-durable
- Description: "Durable conversation, task, and document runtime for Pi". Its README marks it "Experimental. The API changes without notice between releases." T
- Other packages share the 1.4.0 / 2026-10-21 date: `pi-ai`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-coding-agent`, `chord`, `pi-codemode`.
- Runs on Workers. T (README):
  - `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)` from `/storage/sqlite/cloudflare` is the Durable Object SQLite storage.
  - `Harness.open(storage, {models, registry, onWake}, context)` takes an `onWake` hook, so the object can hibernate while tasks sleep.
  - A documented Durable Object class arms an alarm from `harness.wake()`. `alarm()` and the constructor call `harness.resume()`, which picks up work a lost instance left.
- Durability: conversation entries, model turns and tool calls are committed to storage before anything is shown. After a crash or eviction, reopening the storage resumes the work. T (README)
- Effect: not Effect-native. It is a Promise API that takes a Chord `Context` on every call. You would call it from Effect through `Effect.tryPromise`. T
- Tool calling and multi-turn loop: yes. It has a tools set, a registry, tasks, a child-task graph, codemode and subagents. T
- Models: through `@earendil-works/pi-ai`. T
- Vite plugin: none required by the package. T
- Dependencies: `@earendil-works/chord`, `pi-ai`, `pi-codemode`, `pi-telemetry`, `typebox`, `diff`, `@silvia-odwyer/photon`. T
- Related packages: `@netzlabor/pi-durable-postgres` 0.2.0 and `@parcha/pi-durable-disk` 0.1.0-beta.23 (third-party). `pi-durable-telegram` 0.1.5 runs on a server, not Workers. S

**`@earendil-works/pi-ai` and `pi-agent-core` (the model layer today)**
- Latest 1.4.0 (2026-10-21). nagara pins 0.87.0, so it is behind a major version. S
- The `legacy-node20` tag is at 0.74.2. S
- `pi-ai`: unified LLM API with provider objects (`createModels()`, `setProvider(...)`). `pi-agent-core`: agent loop with state management. S
- Gemini and AI Gateway through pi-ai: not verified for 1.4.0.
- Promise-based, not Effect-native.
- Durability: none in itself. `pi-durable` adds it.

**Cloudflare Agents SDK (`agents`)**
- Version 0.30.0, published 2026-10-22. S: https://registry.npmjs.org/agents
- Runs on Workers. Each `Agent` is a Durable Object with SQLite. D
- Not Effect-native. You call it as Promises. Alchemy v2 has Effect wrappers for Durable Objects.
- Multi-turn:
  - `AIChatAgent` is in `@cloudflare/ai-chat`. D
  - Harnesses: `agents/harness/pi`, `ai-sdk`, `opencode`, `think`, `container`. T (package exports)
- Pi harness:
  - `PiHarness` hosts pi-durable inside the Agent's Durable Object SQLite and wakes sessions after eviction. D: `docs/harnesses/pi.md` in the tarball.
  - Beta. `agents` pins `@earendil-works/pi-durable`, `pi-ai` and `chord` at `~1.4.0` as optional peers.
- Workflows:
  - `AgentWorkflow` from `agents` integrates Cloudflare Workflows. D (README)
  - The Agents docs also describe `runFiber`-style durable execution with `ctx.stash` / `ctx.snapshot` checkpoints. D: `docs/durable-execution.md`
  - I did not check whether a conversation id can be set from a Workflow instance id, as nagara does with Flue today.
- Gemini and AI Gateway:
  - `agents/models/pi-ai`: `createAI({binding: env.AI})` returns a pi-ai provider routed through AI Gateway. Model strings use the gateway catalog, e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8` and `dynamic/<route>`. D: `docs/models-pi-ai.md`, `docs/models.md`
  - The gateway defaults to `default` and can be set by the `gateway` option. A key stored on the gateway (BYOK) works. D
  - A Gemini model through it was not tried.
- Vite plugin: the package's peer dependencies list `vite`. `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` is not required by the package. T

**`@effect/ai` v4 (inside `effect`)**
- In v4 the AI modules live in the `effect` package, at `effect/ai`. Package `effect` 4.0.6 (latest, 2026-10-22); `rc` is 4.0.0-rc.118. T / S
- Modules in `effect/ai`: `LanguageModel`, `Chat`, `Toolkit`, `Tool`, `Prompt`, `Response`, `AiError`, `McpServer`, `McpClient`, `EmbeddingModel`. T
- `Chat` has `Chat.Persistence`, `makePersisted` and `layerPersisted`, plus `fromExport` and `fromJson`. T
- The `@effect/ai` 0.37.x / `@effect/ai-google` 0.16.x npm packages are the v3 line. They peer on `effect ^3.22`. S
- The `effect-smol` repo has provider packages `anthropic`, `openai`, `openai-compat` and `openrouter` under `packages/ai`. S
- v4 providers on npm: `@effect/ai-openai`, `@effect/ai-anthropic`, `@effect/ai-openai-compat` and `@effect/ai-openrouter`, all at 4.0.6 (2026-10-22). `ai-openai-compat` peers on `effect ^4.0.6`. S / T
- No v4 Google/Gemini package exists on npm. A Google Vertex AI provider PR (#2377) is closed. S: https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect-smol/pull/2377
- A Gemini model can be reached through the `openai-compat` client pointed at Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or through AI Gateway's compat endpoint. Neither was tried.
- `OpenAiClient` in `openai-compat` takes `apiUrl` and `transformClient`, so the base URL and gateway headers can be set. T (type declarations)
- Effect-native. Tool-call resolution and the multi-turn loop are in `LanguageModel` / `Toolkit` (not run). T
- No Durable Object persistence of its own. `Chat.Persistence` takes a `BackingPersistence` layer, so the backing store is pluggable.
- Vite plugin: none. Runs on Workers because it uses `HttpClient` / `fetch`.
- An AI Gateway provider package under `effect/ai`: none found.

**Alchemy (`alchemy` 2.0.0-beta.83, 2026-10-12)**
- Peers on `effect ^4.0.0`. T: https://registry.npmjs.org/alchemy
- Source (`src/Cloudflare/AI/`): `LanguageModel.ts`, `Gateway.ts`, `GatewayProvider.ts`, `ProviderKey.ts`, `QueryGateway.ts`, `QueryGatewayBinding.ts`, `GatewayDynamicRouting.ts`. T
- `Cloudflare.AI.LanguageModel` is an `effect/ai` `LanguageModel` adapter over the Workers AI `ai.run`, optionally through an AI Gateway id. T
- `DurableObjectChatPersistence` is a `Layer` providing `BackingPersistence` for `effect/ai/Chat`, backed by Durable Object storage. T
- `ProviderKey` manages gateway BYOK keys. T
- `src/AI/Agent.ts`: an `Agent` definition with tools and `send({input, session})`. Its implementation was not read.
- Whether the `LanguageModel` adapter supports Gemini models through `ai.run` was not read.

**Cross-cutting**
- Effect v4 has no Gemini provider package. Gemini through the Gateway has to go over an OpenAI-compatible or custom client.
- pi-durable, `agents` and pi-ai all take Promises and tools defined in their own formats, not Effect `Tool` / `Toolkit`.
- Flue at the time of the check is 2.3.0 (2026-10-12). nagara runs 2.1.0.

**Not verified**
- Anything about Gemini through AI Gateway for any option. No request was run.
- No trial was run of `LanguageModel.generateText` with a toolkit loop, `PiHarness`, or an Alchemy agent on Workers. Everything above is from type declarations, source, READMEs and registry metadata.
- Whether pi-ai 1.4.0 has a Gemini provider and a custom base URL.
- Whether the Agents SDK can use a Workflow instance id as its conversation id.
- Whether pi-durable or `PiHarness` needs a Vite plugin or a particular wrangler config. The docs do not say so.
- The bundle size of pi-durable on Workers.

Load mahou:basics first. Then read `.mahou/spike.md` if present.

# Spike

A spike is code written to answer a question. The answer is the product; the code is not. You build it small, run it against reality, and throw it away. It never merges, never the starting point of the real implementation, which gets built clean once the question is settled.

## The process

1. **Name the question.** One design question that reading and asking cannot settle: whether an approach holds, what shape something should take, what actually happens when the real thing runs. A question a document or a scout can answer does not need a spike.

2. **Build the smallest working version of the real thing.** It works, against real inputs, under real conditions. A mock answers nothing. Build only what the question asks about. Build it in the change's scratch folder, at `spikes/<question-slug>/`, so nothing of it touches a repository.

3. **Run it against reality and observe.** Whatever can tell you the answer is the reactor: real data, a real run, a person reacting, another agent attempting the task. You choose the reactor for the spike; it is not prescribed. What happens is the result, and the gap between that and what was expected is usually the finding.

4. **Iterate in rounds under a strategy.** A round changes something and produces an outcome; the outcome settles a decision or sharpens the question, and the next round builds on what settled. Load the strategy for changing things from `references/strategies/` and pick it per spike:

   | Strategy | When |
   |---|---|
   | [One variable per round](references/strategies/one-variable.md) | The question has a working baseline and the rounds narrow in on failures |
   | [Variants in parallel](references/strategies/variants-in-parallel.md) | Several answers could work and only evidence picks between them |

   A spike may invent its own strategy; when one works, it is a candidate for mahou:learn to add here.

5. **Stop when the question is answered.** Record the answer and the findings in the spike's folder. Every surprise is input to the design that follows. The artifacts stay as reference material for whoever builds the real thing.

## Processes and secrets

- Stop only the processes the spike started, by the process id recorded when starting each one. Never `pkill`, `killall` or a kill by pattern: other work on the machine may be running the same program.
- Read secrets from the files that hold them. Never print them or write them into code, logs or findings.
- When the spike needs a credential only the user can create, ask for it. The user writes it to a file in the change's scratch folder with a `!` command, so the value never enters the conversation, and the spike deletes that file when it finishes.

## What a spike never does

It never decides for the user. The spike brings the outcome; the design decisions it raises go back as questions. It never grows a second question. A new question is a new spike. Extracting the real thing from spike code keeps every shortcut the throwaway allowed.

content.content:
# Local pipeline

`pipeline/` runs locally under `pnpm dev` next to the API Worker, and an item reaches it only through the local API: `POST /items` on port 8788 with the key from `api/.dev.vars`, then `GET /items/<id>` until the status is `ready` or `failed`. `docs/technical-design/local-development.md` gives the launch order and explains the tunnel and the shared state folder. The first item of a domain runs the author agent; an item whose recipe fails validation runs the revision agent.

- The agents reach Workers AI through the real `nagara` AI Gateway on the real account, so a local item spends real usage and shows in the gateway's logs. Keep local items to what the check needs. D1, R2, Durable Object and Workflow state stays local, in the shared `.wrangler-state/` at the repository root.
- The key goes in `pipeline/.dev.vars` as `CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY=REDACTED, next to the other secrets `pipeline/.dev.vars.example` names. Git ignores `.dev.vars`.
- The token is a Cloudflare API token with Workers AI Read and AI Gateway Run. The Wrangler login token does not work. The gateway answers 401, code 2009 "Unauthorized", even though the login token carries `ai (write)`.
- The user writes the key into `.dev.vars`, for example with `! $EDITOR pipeline/.dev.vars`. Auto mode stops an agent from copying a credential.
- Run this call from `pipeline/` to check the key before a run. `<account>` is the `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` in `pipeline/wrangler.jsonc`:
  `curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/<account>/nagara/workers-ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $(grep '^CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY='REDACTED'{"model":"@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say ok"}],"max_tokens":5}'`
- `pnpm dev` does not enforce the recipe CPU cap.
# One variable per round

The strategy for narrowing in on failures when a working baseline exists.

Each round changes one thing and re-runs. When the spike's output fails somewhere, fix that failing case alone. The fix must generalize, not special-case the case that happened to fail. After every fix, re-run everything that already passed. A fix that breaks a passing case has to be redone, and only the re-run can see it, because the failing case itself will look solved.

One variable per round keeps cause and effect readable. A round that changes three things produces an outcome nobody can attribute, and the next round builds on a guess.

The loop ends when the whole corpus passes, not when the last failing case does.

Subagent spike: pi-durable replaces Flue? (w45:pD, done):
All five points worked under `wrangler dev`. A crash inside a tool that isn't replay-safe looped without stopping, and pi-durable's restart limit did not catch it. The write-up is in `.scratch/effect-migration/spikes/pi-durable/findings.md`; the code and logs are in the same folder. Nothing was deployed, no Cloudflare resource was created, and nothing in the repo was edited.

**Versions:** pi-durable 1.4.0, pi-ai 1.4.0, chord 1.4.0, effect 4.0.6, wrangler 4.135.0.

1. **Agent loop in a DO, no Vite: worked.** wrangler's own esbuild bundles it: **3118.98 KiB (549.23 KiB gzip)**. The largest parts are the openai SDK (833 KiB) and the anthropic SDK (577 KiB). Both get in because `cloudflareAIGatewayProvider()` registers all three APIs, as nagara's current provider does. The baseline run took 4 model requests: fetch the article, submit (rejected), submit (accepted), final JSON reply.
2. **Real model through the `nagara` gateway: worked.** The account id, gateway id and key are read from `process.env`, so no auth code was needed. pi-ai 1.4.0's GLM entry already has the right `contextWindow`, but `maxTokens`, `thinkingLevelMap` and `supportsReasoningEffort` are still wrong, so I applied nagara's tuning. I did not check on the wire that `reasoning_effort: "low"` was sent.
3. **Caller-chosen id: worked.** I used one DO per id (`getByName`), with the conversation as pi-durable's root conversation inside it. A second call on the same id quoted the first run's rejection reason word for word. Resubmitting an earlier `requestId` returned the settled submission without calling the model.
4. **Resume: worked.** Turns committed before the kill never ran again. What repeated depends on where the kill landed:
   - **Inside a default tool:** the tool was not rerun. The model got an "interrupted" error result and called it again, costing one extra model request.
   - **Mid-stream:** that model request was sent again from scratch. The partial reply stayed in the transcript marked `aborted`, with usage 0, though the gateway still billed it.
   - **Alarm only, no caller retry:** finished the same way. The constructor's `resume()` did the work, because workerd cancelled the `alarm()` handler when the constructor re-armed the alarm.
   - **Tool marked `replay: "safe"`:** the same tool task ran again and no extra model request was needed.
5. **From Effect v4: worked.** The friction:
   - Effect's `Context` and chord's `Context` share a name, so one of them has to be aliased on import.
   - The tool's `api` and chord `Context` arrive with each call, so the Effect service has to be built and provided inside every `execute`.
   - `Schedule.both` does not exist in 4.0.6.

**Surprises:**
- `ctx.abort()` throws away storage writes that have not been flushed. My "already crashed" flag was lost, so every restart crashed again.
- That loop is the one the restart limit missed. Each restart the model made a new tool call, so no single task crashed 5 times. It ran 7 model requests in about 45 s before I stopped wrangler.
- nagara's root workspace overrides pi-ai to 0.87.0, but pi-durable needs exactly 1.4.0. The spike has its own workspace file, so the override did not apply here.
- effect 4.0.6 was published the same day, so pnpm's minimum-release-age rule blocked it until I excluded it in the spike's workspace.

**Gateway calls spent:** 37. That is 1 key check, 7 in the runaway loop, and 29 across the rounds; one was the aborted stream. Each conversation used about 4.5–7.6k tokens.

**Not done:**
- Stopping the wrangler process mid-run (I only used `ctx.abort()`), a deployed run, or a real Workflow calling the DO.
- A real-size article, compaction, the turn budget and output caps.
- Concurrent calls, a failing Effect inside a tool, tests under the vitest plugin, and trimming the bundle.

**Process note:** I stopped the first wrangler with `pkill -P <recorded pid>`, which only targets that pid's children. The second I stopped by killing its listed child pids. No spike processes remain.

pi-durable passed all five spike checks, but a tool that crashes every time made it loop without stopping. It ran locally under `wrangler dev`, deployed nothing, created no Cloudflare resources, and spent 37 real gateway calls. The results are on the canvas next to Q7, and the full write-up is in `/home/agus/workspace/asermax/nagara/.scratch/effect-migration/spikes/pi-durable/findings.md`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Tool loop in a Durable Object, built by wrangler with no Vite plugin | Worked. Bundle is 3.1 MB (549 KiB gzip). Most of it is the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, pulled in because pi-ai's built-in gateway provider registers all three APIs. |
| GLM 5.3 Flash through the real `nagara` gateway | Worked. pi-ai 1.4.0 still needs nagara's limit tuning (`maxTokens`, `thinkingLevelMap`). |
| Conversation keyed by an id the caller chooses | Worked. One Durable Object per id, and the second call saw the first call's history. |
| Resume after the Durable Object is killed | Worked. Turns that were already saved never ran again; where the kill landed decided what repeated. Killed inside a tool, the model got an "interrupted" result and called the tool again, at the cost of one extra request. Killed mid-reply, that one request was sent again, and the gateway still billed the aborted one. |
| Driven from Effect v4 | Worked. Effect's `Context` and pi's `Context` clash by name, and services have to be provided inside each tool call. |

**The loop:** pi-durable's restart limit counts crashes per task. Each restart the model made a new tool call, which is a new task, so the limit never triggered. It ran 7 model requests in about 45 seconds before the spike agent stopped it.

**Not covered:**
- a real Workflow calling the Durable Object
- a deployed run
- a real-size article
- turn budgets
- concurrent calls
- tests under the per-file test environment

**Questions for you:**
- **Q7:** go with pi-durable (option B), or another option?
- **Q8:** what should stop a tool that crashes every time: a request budget per conversation in the agent, the Workflow step's timeout, marking tools as safe to replay, or something else?
- **Q9:** pi-durable needs pi-ai exactly 1.4.0, and nagara pins 0.87.0 across the whole workspace. Should the move include that upgrade? And should the provider register only the one API GLM uses, to drop the two SDKs from the bundle?

Still open from before:
- the two `[?]` rows in the module table: `waitForEvent` and Worker Loaders under Alchemy
- the offer to read the `drizzle-on-d1` wiki entry against the `common/db` row

20-## Layout
21-
22:- `src/agent.ts`: the `AuthorAgent` Durable Object. It opens the Harness on `openDurableObjectSqliteStorage(ctx.storage)` in `blockConcurrencyWhile`, arms the alarm the way the README shows, and calls `harness.resume()` in the constructor and in `alarm()`. `run(message, requestId, crash)` submits to the root conversation and waits. Base directory for this skill: /home/agus/workspace/asermax/claude-plugins/superpowers/skills/mermaid # Mermaid Diagrams Use a diagram to show something that prose would explain worse: a data model, a flow across services or APIs, a state lifecycle, an object structure. A diagram is worth drawing when the subject has many parts, branches, an order over time or a structure. Do not diagram something one sentence explains. ## How to use this skill 1. Pick the chart type from the chart-selection table below. 2. Open the matching `references/*.md` for that chart's syntax, a worked example and its styling guidance. Load only the references you need. 3. Write the diagram following the common syntax rules. In a flowchart or a state diagram, take each element's shape and colour from the palette in [references/flowchart.md](references/flowchart.md). 4. Validate it, then render it and look at the image (see Validation). Both steps are mandatory. 5. Place the diagram next to the prose it illustrates, not in a separate "diagrams" section. ## Chart selection | You're documenting | Chart | Reference | |---|---|---| | A data model, a schema, database changes (entities, fields, relationships) | `erDiagram` | [references/er-diagram.md](references/er-diagram.md) | | Branching logic, request routing, a flow across a repository's services | `flowchart` | [references/flowchart.md](references/flowchart.md) | | Interaction over time across actors, services or APIs (who calls whom, in what order) | `sequenceDiagram` | [references/sequence-diagram.md](references/sequence-diagram.md) | | The lifecycle or status transitions of an entity | `stateDiagram-v2` | [references/state-diagram.md](references/state-diagram.md) | | Object and type structure and relationships (classes, DTO hierarchies, interfaces) | `classDiagram` | [references/class-diagram.md](references/class-diagram.md) | When two charts fit, such as a flow that could be a `flowchart` or a `sequenceDiagram`, use `sequenceDiagram` when who acts and the order of messages matter, and `flowchart` when branches and decisions matter more than order. ## Common syntax - **Start every diagram with a type declaration**: `flowchart TD`, `sequenceDiagram`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `erDiagram`, `classDiagram`. A block without one does not render. - **Direction** (flowchart and state diagram): `TD` or `TB` runs top-down, `LR` left to right, `BT` bottom-up and `RL` right to left. Use `LR` for pipelines and flows, `TD` for trees and decisions. - **Quote labels with special characters.** Quote any label that contains `()`, `[]`, `{}`, `:`, `,` or quotes: `A["Process (step 1)"]`. Unquoted special characters cause most parse failures. - **Define a node once, then refer to it by id.** Give a node its shape and label on first use (`A[Start]`), then write only `A`. - **Comments** start with `%%` on their own line. - **Leave out decoration and any detail the reader does not need.** ## Validation (mandatory) Diagrams are drawn with [pele](https://pele.run), a renderer that reads mermaid syntax with its own layout engine and visual style. Its syntax is strict, and an invalid diagram renders as an error box instead of a drawing. Validate every diagram before you show it. Write the diagram to a temp file and feed the file to the validator; do not pass a multi-line diagram as an inline shell string, because shell quoting breaks it and the validator reports errors that are not in the diagram. 1. **Write** the raw diagram body (the text between the ` ```mermaid ` fences, without the fences) to a temp file with the `Write` tool, such as `/tmp/diagram.mmd`. 2. **Run** the validator, which reads the diagram from stdin and, given an output path, also renders it to a PNG: ```bash bash /home/agus/workspace/asermax/claude-plugins/superpowers/skills/mermaid/scripts/validate-mermaid.sh /tmp/diagram.png < /tmp/diagram.mmd ``` 3. **Read the result.** The script prints JSON; check `isValid` and `errors[]`: ```json { "isValid": false, "diagramType": "flowchart", "errors": [ { "code": "syntax", "line": 3, "column": 1, "message": "Parse error on line 3: ^ Expecting 'SQE', 'UNICODE_TEXT', 'TEXT', 'TAGSTART', got '$end'" } ] } ``` `code` is one of `syntax`, `semantic`, `unsupported-diagram` and `limit`. Exit codes: `0` valid, `1` invalid, `2` setup error. 4. If the diagram is invalid, **fix** it using the `line` and `message` of each error, then run the validator again until `isValid` is `true`. 5. **Look** at the rendered `/tmp/diagram.png` with the `Read` tool before you show the diagram. A diagram that parses can still draw wrong (see Rendering rules the validator cannot catch). Check for stray nodes or states, overlapping text, and a layout far wider or taller than the page. The script calls pele's own `render()`, so a diagram it accepts is one every pele renderer draws, and the PNG is pele's SVG rasterized with resvg using pele's default light theme. It installs both packages on first run into `~/.cache/claude-plugins/pele/`. Frontmatter and `%%{init}%%` directives are passed to pele, which reads them. ### Fixing common errors - **Unquoted labels with special characters**: wrap them in quotes, `A["Total (USD)"]`, `B{"valid?"}`. - **Wrong arrow for the diagram type**: `-->` in flowcharts, `->>`/`-->>` in sequence diagrams, `-->` in state and class diagrams. Mixing them fails. - **Missing type declaration**: the first line that is not a comment must declare the diagram type. - **`subgraph` or `state` block without its end**: every `subgraph` needs an `end`, and every composite `state X {` needs its `}`. - **A node's shape declared twice**: declare the shape once; later references use the bare id. - **Reserved word as a bare node id**: `end`, `class` and similar ids break parsing; rename the node or quote it. ## Rendering rules the validator cannot catch The parser accepts these, and the renderer draws them wrong. # Sequence Diagram ## When to use Interactions over time across actors, services or APIs: who calls whom, in what order, and what comes back. Use it for a request flow that spans a frontend, a BFF or consumer API, and one or more data APIs. For branching logic with no order in time, use a [flowchart](flowchart.md). ## Key syntax - Declare the type: `sequenceDiagram`. - **Participants**: `actor U as User` for people (a stick figure); `participant S as Service` for systems (a box). Declaring them first fixes their left-to-right order. - **Messages**: `->>` solid call, `-->>` dashed return, `-x` lost message. Always give a label after the colon: `U->>S: GET /courses`. - **Activations** (the bar that shows a participant is working): append `+` to the arrow to activate the target and `-` to deactivate it on return, `Alice->>+John: request` then `John-->>-Alice: response`. Or write `activate John` and `deactivate John`. - **Fragments**: `alt`/`else` (conditional), `opt` (optional), `loop` (repeat), `par`/`and` (parallel). Each closes with `end`. - **Notes**: `Note over A,B: text`, `Note right of A: text`. - **`autonumber`** numbers every message. ## Worked example ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor U as User participant BFF as Consumer API participant API as Courses API participant DB as Postgres Note over U,API: Authenticated fetch U->>+BFF: GET /courses BFF->>+API: GET /internal/courses API->>DB: SELECT ... DB-->>API: rows API-->>-BFF: courses[] BFF-->>-U: 200 courses[] alt no enrollment U->>BFF: POST /enroll BFF-->>U: 201 created else already enrolled BFF-->>U: 409 conflict end ``` ## Styling guidance - **Draw people as `actor` and systems as `participant`.** - **Use activations** to show which participant is working and when control returns. Write them with the `+`/`-` shorthand on the messages so each activation has its end. - **Group a phase with `rect`**: wrap the messages of one phase in a coloured background, with a `Note over` that names it: ``` rect rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.15) Note over U,API: Phase 1, request ... end ``` Use a different translucent colour per phase; an alpha of about 0.15 to 0.25 keeps the messages readable. `rect` blocks can nest. - **Use `autonumber`** when the prose refers to steps by number. - **Declare participants in the order they should appear** so message lines cross as little as possible. - **Break long notes with `
`.** Notes do not wrap; see the rendering rules in `SKILL.md`.

Subagent scout: recipe step agent flow (w45:pE, done):
The recipe step reads the domain's latest saved recipe from D1 and runs it through the sandbox runtime. If there is none, or it fails, `settle()` starts a Flue agent conversation: the author when no recipe exists, the revisor when the saved one failed. The agent's reply is only a settled script, a `not-article` verdict or `gave-up`. `converge()` runs any script through the same sandbox runtime again before the step persists it.

**Step and retry config**
- `ItemWorkflow.run` calls `fetchStep`, `leaseStep`, then `recipeStep(ctx, domain, html)` (`pipeline/src/workflow/item.ts:78-82`), then `releaseStep`, `imagesStep` and the rest.
- The recipe step is `runStep(ctx, STEP.recipe, "generating", "15 minutes", …)` (`pipeline/src/workflow/steps/recipe.ts:16`), and `STEP.recipe` is `"recipe"` (`common/src/workflow.ts:8`).
- `STEP_RETRIES` is `{limit: 2, delay: "5 seconds", backoff: "exponential"}`, which gives 3 attempts (`pipeline/src/workflow/wrapper.ts:13-17`).
- Each attempt writes `status=generating, currentStep=recipe` before the body runs (`wrapper.ts:46`). On final failure, `failStep` runs a `"recipe failed"` step that writes `status=failed` (`wrapper.ts:24-31, 51`).
- The page HTML comes from `fetchStep` (Firecrawl scrape, `pipeline/src/workflow/steps/fetch.ts:16,38`). It is capped at `maxHtmlBytes` of 1 MiB and passed to the recipe step as an argument.

**Recipe step body** (`recipe.ts:17-39`)
1. `getLatestRecipeVersion(db, domain)` reads `recipe_versions` for the domain's highest version. This is the only D1 read before the agents.
2. `settle(env, {instanceId, domain, html, recipe})` runs.
3. `not-article` and `gave-up` both throw `NonRetryableError` (`recipe.ts:22-28`). The step fails at once without retrying, because the agents already used their own retries (comment at `recipe.ts:13-14`).
4. On `ok`, `toTypedUnits(settled.units)` runs, then `updateItem` writes `title`, `units` and `recipe_version_id` (`recipe.ts:30-37`).
5. `recipe_version_id` is the existing version id, or a new `createRecipeVersion(db, {domain, script})` row when `versionId` is null (a script the agents just settled). The step returns `{declaredImages}`.

**`settle` and `converge`** (`pipeline/src/recipes/settle.ts`)
- **No recipe** (`:74-82`): `converge` with `agent:"author"`, `retries: env.authoringRetries` (1), `authorMessage(domain, null)`.
- **Recipe present** (`:84-95`): `runRecipe(env, recipe.script, html)` runs first. If it is `ok`, it returns `versionId: recipe.id` and no agent runs.
- **Recipe present and failing** (`:96-102`): `converge` with `agent:"revision"`, `retries: env.revisionRetries` (2), `report: run.report`, and `revisionMessage(domain, report ?? run.report, recipe.script)`.
- **Loop** (`:40-66`): `for attempt 0..retries` calls `agentConversation(agent, instanceId, message(report), {html, recipe: recipe?.script})`, so there are `retries+1` agent calls.
- **Reply handling** (`:45-64`):
  - `parseSettlement(reply)`: `not-article` returns at once.
  - `script`: `runRecipe(env, settlement.source, html)`. If `run.ok`, it returns `{ok, title, units, script, versionId:null}`; otherwise `report = run.report` and the loop continues with that report.
  - `gave-up` or an unparseable reply: the loop continues with the same report.
- **Exhausted** (`:68`): `gave-up` with the `exhausted` string. For the author it is "authoring gave up: nothing is saved for the domain"; for revision it is "revision gave up: …the old version stands".
- Because `createRecipeVersion` only runs after a `settle()` success (`recipe.ts:35-36`), a failed revision writes no version.

**`conversation.ts` and `gateway.ts`**
- `agentConversation` calls `dispatchAgent`, then `readAgent(...).text` (`pipeline/src/agents/conversation.ts:9-16`).
- `dispatchAgent` does `init(agentFor(kind), {id: conversationId}).dispatch({message, initialData})` and returns a receipt `{submissionId, acceptedAt, uid}` (`pipeline/src/agents/gateway.ts:138-146`).
- `readAgent` does `init(...).read(receipt)` and returns `{text}` (`gateway.ts:148-156`).
- `initialDataFor` (`gateway.ts:129-136`) gives the author `{html}` and the revisor `{html, recipe}`.
- The `agentConversation` call is not wrapped in a Workflow step of its own. Dispatch and read both happen inside the recipe step's single `step.do`, so a step retry runs `settle()` again from the top.
- The conversation id is `instanceId` alone, so every retry or restart from the recipe step reuses the same Flue agent instance and its history (`settle.ts:30-32`; `docs/technical-design/item-lifecycle.md:307`).
- The author and the revisor are separate Durable Object classes (`FlueAuthorAgent`, `FlueRevisorAgent`, `pipeline/wrangler.jsonc:23-24`). Because both use the same conversation id, an item that moves between them would not share history.

**Author** (`pipeline/src/agents/author.ts`)
- **Model:** `useModel(env.agentModel, {thinkingLevel:"off"})` (`:12`). `agentModel` is glm-5.3-flash through AI Gateway (`wrangler.jsonc:28`). `off` is mapped to reasoning_effort `low` (`pipeline/src/agents/model-provider.ts:241-243`).
- **Input:** `useInitialData` gives `{html}` (`:13`), passed from the step's fetched HTML. The instruction is `authorInstruction(env.agentMaxTurns, html)` (`:15`): the HTML is embedded in the system prompt (`pipeline/src/agents/prompts.ts:39-45, 47-60`), and the dispatch message is `authorMessage` (`prompts.ts:81-90`).
- **Tool:** `useExtractTool(html)` registers one tool.
- **Durability:** `AGENT_DURABILITY = {maxAttempts: 5, timeoutMs: 1_800_000}`, i.e. 30 minutes (`pipeline/src/agents/extract-tool.ts:7`).
- **Output:** one fenced json block. `REPLY_CONTRACT` (`prompts.ts:27-37`) allows `{kind:"script", source}`, `{kind:"not-article"}` or `{kind:"gave-up", reason}`. `parseSettlement` (`pipeline/src/agents/settlement.ts:34-47`) takes the last fenced block that validates, else the whole text, else `gave-up`.

**Revisor** (`pipeline/src/agents/revisor.ts`)
- Same shape as the author with two differences:
  - Its initial data is `{html, recipe}` (`:8-11`), though the recipe is not used in the instruction. It arrives in the dispatch message through `revisionMessage` (`prompts.ts:92-102`), together with the validator report.
  - Its instruction is additive: keep the previous assumptions, and rewrite outright only on a redesign (`prompts.ts:63-79`).
- It has the same tool, model and durability. A `not-article` verdict writes no version (`prompts.ts:74`).

**The `extract` tool** (`extract-tool.ts:10-23`)
- Input is `{recipe: string}` and the output is a `RecipeRun`: `{ok, title, units}` or `{ok:false, report}`.
- `run` calls `runRecipe(env, data.recipe, html)` with the closed-over HTML.
- It reaches the recipe runtime through the `LOADER` Worker Loader binding. It does not touch D1, R2 or `fetch`.

**Deterministic runtime** (`pipeline/src/runtime/run.ts`)
- **Execution:** `executeInDynamicWorker` calls `env.LOADER.load` with `runtime.js`, `injection.js` and `recipe.js`, `limits.cpuMs = env.recipeCpuMs` (2000) and `globalOutbound: null`, so the sandbox has no network access (`run.ts:120-130`). It sends a `GET /health` probe, then `POST /extract` with `{html}` (`run.ts:142, 175-181`).
- **Failure reports:** a recipe that fails to load, parse or execute comes back as `{ok:false, report}` (`run.ts:148-152, 166-169, 190-193`). A `PlatformFailure` is thrown for an unloadable runtime or an unreachable dynamic worker (`run.ts:132, 171, 183`).
- **Validation:** `runRecipe` calls `validateExtraction(extraction, html)`. A non-empty report returns `{ok:false, report}`, otherwise `{title, units: units.map(toBoundaryUnit)}` (`run.ts:206-211`).
- This is invariant 10: both the agent's tool calls and the final settled script go through this same `runRecipe`.

**Budgets**
- **Turns:** `agentMaxTurns` is 100 (`wrangler.jsonc:31`). It is only stated in the prompt ("about N turns", `prompts.ts:54, 72`). I found no code that enforces it.
- **Agent retries:** `authoringRetries` is 1 and `revisionRetries` is 2 (`wrangler.jsonc:32-33`).
- **Agent timeouts:** each agent has 5 durability attempts and a 30-minute timeout (`extract-tool.ts:7`). That is longer than the recipe step's 15-minute `step.do` timeout.
- **Recipe CPU:** 2000 ms per run.

**Persisted**
- `recipe_versions` has `id` (`rcp_…`), `domain`, `version`, `script`, `created_at`, with `unique(domain, version)` (`common/src/db/schema.ts:36-47`). `createRecipeVersion` is a pure insert, so two concurrent saves collide on the unique pair instead of sharing a number (`common/src/db/recipe-versions/create-recipe-version.ts`).
- `items.recipe_version_id` references it (`schema.ts:66`). Only a successful settle writes the item's `title`, `units` and `recipe_version_id`.
- Agent conversation history is held in the Flue Durable Objects keyed by `instanceId`.

**Not found or unclear**
- **Turn cap:** no code enforces the 100-turn limit, only the prompt text. Flue's own limit, if any, is in `@flue/runtime`, outside this repo.
- **Version numbering:** I did not trace where `version` gets its next value, and `createRecipeVersion` passes only `domain` and `script`. It is probably a migration default or trigger.
- **Retried dispatch:** a step retry calls `dispatch` again with a new message on the same conversation. How `@flue/runtime` handles repeated dispatches with the same `id` is not in this repo. The docs link is `docs/technical-design/item-lifecycle.md:362`.

The recipe step reads the domain's latest saved recipe from D1 and runs it through the sandbox runtime. If there is none, or it fails, `settle()` starts a Flue agent conversation: the author when no recipe exists, the revisor when the saved one failed. The agent's reply is only a settled script, a `not-article` verdict or `gave-up`. `converge()` runs any script through the same sandbox runtime again before the step persists it.

**Step and retry config**
- `ItemWorkflow.run` calls `fetchStep`, `leaseStep`, then `recipeStep(ctx, domain, html)` (`pipeline/src/workflow/item.ts:78-82`), then `releaseStep`, `imagesStep` and the rest.
- The recipe step is `runStep(ctx, STEP.recipe, "generating", "15 minutes", …)` (`pipeline/src/workflow/steps/recipe.ts:16`), and `STEP.recipe` is `"recipe"` (`common/src/workflow.ts:8`).
- `STEP_RETRIES` is `{limit: 2, delay: "5 seconds", backoff: "exponential"}`, which gives 3 attempts (`pipeline/src/workflow/wrapper.ts:13-17`).
- Each attempt writes `status=generating, currentStep=recipe` before the body runs (`wrapper.ts:46`). On final failure, `failStep` runs a `"recipe failed"` step that writes `status=failed` (`wrapper.ts:24-31, 51`).
- The page HTML comes from `fetchStep` (Firecrawl scrape, `pipeline/src/workflow/steps/fetch.ts:16,38`). It is capped at `maxHtmlBytes` of 1 MiB and passed to the recipe step as an argument.

**Recipe step body** (`recipe.ts:17-39`)
1. `getLatestRecipeVersion(db, domain)` reads `recipe_versions` for the domain's highest version. This is the only D1 read before the agents.
2. `settle(env, {instanceId, domain, html, recipe})` runs.
3. `not-article` and `gave-up` both throw `NonRetryableError` (`recipe.ts:22-28`). The step fails at once without retrying, because the agents already used their own retries (comment at `recipe.ts:13-14`).
4. On `ok`, `toTypedUnits(settled.units)` runs, then `updateItem` writes `title`, `units` and `recipe_version_id` (`recipe.ts:30-37`).
5. `recipe_version_id` is the existing version id, or a new `createRecipeVersion(db, {domain, script})` row when `versionId` is null (a script the agents just settled). The step returns `{declaredImages}`.

**`settle` and `converge`** (`pipeline/src/recipes/settle.ts`)
- **No recipe** (`:74-82`): `converge` with `agent:"author"`, `retries: env.authoringRetries` (1), `authorMessage(domain, null)`.
- **Recipe present** (`:84-95`): `runRecipe(env, recipe.script, html)` runs first. If it is `ok`, it returns `versionId: recipe.id` and no agent runs.
- **Recipe present and failing** (`:96-102`): `converge` with `agent:"revision"`, `retries: env.revisionRetries` (2), `report: run.report`, and `revisionMessage(domain, report ?? run.report, recipe.script)`.
- **Loop** (`:40-66`): `for attempt 0..retries` calls `agentConversation(agent, instanceId, message(report), {html, recipe: recipe?.script})`, so there are `retries+1` agent calls.
- **Reply handling** (`:45-64`):
  - `parseSettlement(reply)`: `not-article` returns at once.
  - `script`: `runRecipe(env, settlement.source, html)`. If `run.ok`, it returns `{ok, title, units, script, versionId:null}`; otherwise `report = run.report` and the loop continues with that report.
  - `gave-up` or an unparseable reply: the loop continues with the same report.
- **Exhausted** (`:68`): `gave-up` with the `exhausted` string. For the author it is "authoring gave up: nothing is saved for the domain"; for revision it is "revision gave up: …the old version stands".
- Because `createRecipeVersion` only runs after a `settle()` success (`recipe.ts:35-36`), a failed revision writes no version.

**`conversation.ts` and `gateway.ts`**
- `agentConversation` calls `dispatchAgent`, then `readAgent(...).text` (`pipeline/src/agents/conversation.ts:9-16`).
- `dispatchAgent` does `init(agentFor(kind), {id: conversationId}).dispatch({message, initialData})` and returns a receipt `{submissionId, acceptedAt, uid}` (`pipeline/src/agents/gateway.ts:138-146`).
- `readAgent` does `init(...).read(receipt)` and returns `{text}` (`gateway.ts:148-156`).
- `initialDataFor` (`gateway.ts:129-136`) gives the author `{html}` and the revisor `{html, recipe}`.
- The `agentConversation` call is not wrapped in a Workflow step of its own. Dispatch and read both happen inside the recipe step's single `step.do`, so a step retry runs `settle()` again from the top.
- The conversation id is `instanceId` alone, so every retry or restart from the recipe step reuses the same Flue agent instance and its history (`settle.ts:30-32`; `docs/technical-design/item-lifecycle.md:307`).

The sequence diagram is on the canvas, to the right of the spike result. It shows how the recipe step would use pi-durable. The diagram is a proposal I built from the spike and from a scout's trace of today's recipe step. Only the trace of today's code is verified.

**The flow:**
1. The recipe step reads the domain's saved recipe and runs it in the recipe runtime. If it works, the step saves the item and no agent runs.
2. If there is no recipe, or it fails, the step calls the agent's Durable Object by the Workflow instance id. It sends the message, the page HTML and a request id.
3. Inside the object, pi-durable loops through model turns to GLM via AI Gateway. Each `extract` tool call runs the candidate recipe in the recipe runtime.
4. It returns a script, `not-article` or `gave-up`. If the object is evicted mid-turn, it resumes from its constructor or alarm without rerunning saved turns.
5. A returned script runs through the recipe runtime once more, as invariant 10 requires, and then the step saves the recipe version and the item. `not-article` or `gave-up` ends the step without retrying.

**How today differs**, from the scout's trace:
- **Step retries:** a retried step reruns the whole settle flow and sends a new message on the same Flue conversation.
- **Retry loop:** the step loops around the agent call: the author gets 1 retry and the revisor 2, and each retry gets the runtime's failure report.
- **Two agent classes:** author and revisor are separate Durable Object classes, so they share no history.
- **Budgets:** the agent timeout is 30 minutes against the step's 15. The 100-turn budget exists only as text in the prompt; no code enforces it.

**New questions:**
- **Q10:** what should a retried step send? With a request id that stays the same per attempt, the retry gets the already-settled reply back without a model call, as seen in the spike. With a new id per attempt, the retry continues the conversation with a new message, as Flue does today.
- **Q11:** keep author and revisor as two Durable Object classes, or use one object per item where the revisor can read the author's history?
- **Q12:** keep the retry loop in the recipe step around the agent call, or move it into the agent so the step makes one call?

Q7 is still open: is pi-durable the replacement for Flue?

# Harness

 - Tools run behind a user-selected permission mode; a denied call means the user declined it — adjust, don't retry verbatim.

Each block's opening and closing tags carry the same random id; the user never sees the id, so don't mention it when referring to the pasted text.

The calls run in the order sent, so the publish sends the edited file; a publish sent in the same response as a failed Edit of that file is refused and leaves the artifact as it was, so correct the Edit and publish again.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. WebSearch takes a `mode`. Use "standard" by default: it is the normal search, quick and cheap. Use "extended" only when a "standard" result comes back thin, off-target or possibly outdated, or from the start for hard-to-find or niche facts, very recent events, prices and availability, and multi-step research: it is thorough and fresh but several times the cost.
